# Tobit Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** This is the book of the acts of Tobit son of Tobiel son of Ananiel son of Aduel son of Gabael son of Raphael son of Raguel, from the lineage of Asiel, of the tribe of Naphtali,

**1:2** who was taken captive in the days of Enemessar king of the Assyrians, from Thisbe, which lies to the south of Kedesh-Naphtali in upper Galilee, above Asher, toward the west, near the ridge of Phogor.

**1:3** I, Tobit, walked in the paths of truth and in righteous deeds all the days of my life. And I performed many acts of mercy for my kindred and my people who had gone with me into exile in the land of the Assyrians, to Nineveh.

**1:4** When I was still in my own land, in the land of Israel — while I was yet young — the whole tribe of Naphtali, my ancestor's people, broke away from the house of Jerusalem, which had been chosen out of all the tribes of Israel as the place where all the tribes should offer sacrifice, where the temple of the dwelling of the Most High had been consecrated and built for all generations of the age.

**1:5** All the tribes that had revolted with them, along with the house of Jeroboam my forefather, were sacrificing to Baal the calf.

**1:6** But I alone made the journey to Jerusalem often, for the appointed feasts, as it is prescribed as an everlasting ordinance for all Israel, bringing with me the firstfruits and the tithes of my produce and the firstborn animals and the first shearings of the sheep,

**1:7** and I would give them to the priests, the sons of Aaron, at the altar. The tithe of grain, wine, olive oil, pomegranates, figs, and the rest of the fruit I gave to the sons of Levi who ministered in Jerusalem. The second tithe I would convert to silver for six years, and then go up to Jerusalem and spend it there each year.

**1:8** The third tithe I gave to the orphans and the widows and to the resident aliens who had attached themselves to the children of Israel. I brought it and gave it every third year, and we ate it in accordance with the ordinance prescribed in the law of Moses, according to the commands that Deborah the mother of our ancestor Ananiel had laid upon us — for my father had died and left me an orphan.

**1:9** When I came of age I took a wife from our own family's lineage; her name was Anna, and she bore me a son whom I named Tobias.

**1:10** After I was taken captive to Assyria and arrived as a prisoner at Nineveh, all my kindred and countrymen ate the food of the Gentiles,

**1:11** but I kept strict watch over myself and would not eat,

**1:12** for I kept God always in mind with my whole soul.

**1:13** The Most High granted me favor and good standing in the eyes of Enemessar, and I became his purchasing agent.

**1:14** I traveled to Media and made purchases for him until he died. I also deposited ten talents of silver in trust with Gabael the brother of Gabrias, in the region of Media.

**1:15** When Enemessar died, his son Sennacherib reigned in his place. The roads through Media became impassable, and I could no longer travel there.

**1:16** In the days of Enemessar I performed many acts of mercy for my kindred:

**1:17** I gave my bread to the hungry and my clothing to the naked; and whenever I found any of my people dead and thrown out on the walls of Nineveh, I buried them.

**1:18** And when Sennacherib returned in flight from Judea — in the days of the judgment that the King of Heaven brought upon him for the blasphemies he had uttered — and he was killing many of the Israelites, I buried their bodies in secret. For in his rage he was putting many to death, and I would steal their corpses away and bury them; Sennacherib searched for them and could not find them.

**1:19** Then a certain Ninevite went and informed the king that I was the one burying them. When I learned that I had been denounced to the king and that my life was being sought, I was afraid and fled.

**1:20** Everything I possessed was seized; nothing was left to me except my wife Anna and my son Tobias.

**1:21** But before forty days had passed, two of his own sons murdered him, and they fled to the mountains of Ararat. His son Sarchedonus reigned in his place, and he appointed Achiacharus son of my brother Anael over all the financial accounts of his kingdom and over the entire administration.

**1:22** Achiacharus interceded for me, and I returned to Nineveh. Now Achiacharus had been chief cupbearer, keeper of the royal signet ring, steward, and treasurer; Sarchedonus had made him second in authority. He was my nephew, and he was family.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

- All three translators agreed that this chapter establishes Tobit as an exemplary observer of Torah before the narrative trials begin. The catalogue of tithes and charity is deliberate self-characterization.
- "Acts of mercy" (eleēmosynas) is SOPHIA's consistent rendering throughout Tobit, following LOGOS's lead. This term carries almsgiving, burial of the dead, and covenant loyalty simultaneously.
- "The Most High" is consistently preferred over "God" as a divine title in Tobit.
- The three translators agreed on the historical anchoring: Enemessar = Shalmaneser V; Sennacherib; Sarchedonus = Esarhaddon.
- SOPHIA retains "Sarchedonus" rather than PNEUMA's "Esarhaddon" for formal consistency with the source text naming convention.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### TOB 1:2 — Geographic Orientation
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "to the right of Kedesh of Naphtali" |
| LOGOS | "to the south of Kedesh-Naphtali" |
| PNEUMA | "on the southern edge of Kedesh-Naphtali" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "to the south of Kedesh-Naphtali" (LOGOS). The Greek ek dexiōn in geographic contexts conventionally means "to the south" when facing east. LOGOS and PNEUMA agree on directional meaning; EMET's literal "to the right" obscures the spatial reference for English readers.

### TOB 1:3 — Register of Opening
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "I, Tobit, walked in ways of truth and in righteous-deeds" |
| LOGOS | "I, Tobit, walked in the paths of truth and righteous deeds" |
| PNEUMA | "My name is Tobit, and all my life I tried to walk a straight path" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS (with minor adjustment). PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the formal "I, Tobit" self-presentation and the exact phrase "paths of truth" which echoes wisdom literature. EMET's hyphenation is overly mechanical.

### TOB 1:5 — The Idol
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "to the heifer Baal" |
| LOGOS | "to the calf of Baal" |
| PNEUMA | "to the golden calf of Baal" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "to Baal the calf" — splits the difference. The Greek has damali tō Baal ("to the heifer/calf, the Baal"). LOGOS is more accurate on the noun ("calf" over "heifer" which implies female). PNEUMA adds "golden" with no textual basis.

### TOB 1:6 — Tobit's Pilgrimage Habit
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "I alone was-going-up often to Jerusalem" |
| LOGOS | "I alone would frequently go up to Jerusalem" |
| PNEUMA | "Every year…I made the journey to Jerusalem alone" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. PNEUMA's "every year" is interpretive and conflicts with "often" (pollakis = frequently, not necessarily annual). EMET's hyphenated constructions here impede readability.

### TOB 1:13 — Tobit's Role
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "his purchasing-agent" |
| LOGOS | "his purveyor" |
| PNEUMA | "the king's personal purchasing agent" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** "his purchasing agent" — EMET and PNEUMA agree on the sense; LOGOS's "purveyor" is archaic. SOPHIA drops the hyphen and PNEUMA's "personal" (not in the Greek).

### TOB 1:18 — Attribution of Judgment
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "in-the days of the-judgment that-the-King of Heaven executed upon him" |
| LOGOS | "in the days of the judgment that the King of Heaven brought upon him" |
| PNEUMA | "the catastrophe that God brought on him for his arrogance and blasphemy" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "King of Heaven" is the Tobit text's own title and must be preserved. PNEUMA's substitution of "God" and addition of "arrogance" are interpretive expansions. EMET is accurate but awkward.

### TOB 1:21 — Succession and Murder
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "two of his sons killed him and they-fled to the mountains of Ararat" |
| LOGOS | "two of his sons murdered him and fled to the mountains of Ararat" |
| PNEUMA | "two of Sennacherib's own sons stabbed him in his sleep and fled" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Murdered" is the more precise legal/moral term for deliberate killing. PNEUMA's "stabbed him in his sleep" adds vivid detail not in the text.

### TOB 1:22 — Achiacharus's Roles
| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "chief-cup-bearer and keeper-of-the-ring and steward and accountant" |
| LOGOS | "chief cupbearer, keeper of the signet ring, steward, and treasurer" |
| PNEUMA | "chief cupbearer, keeper of the royal seal, steward, treasurer" |
**SOPHIA's Resolution:** LOGOS. "Signet ring" is more precise than "royal seal" (PNEUMA). "Treasurer" is preferable to EMET's "accountant" for the Greek oikonomos context.
